discovery: Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated electron systems

nominees.name: Antoine Georges
nominees.affiliation: Collège de France, Paris, and Flatiron Institute, New York

motivation: Vollhardt (with Metzner) showed that the lattice problem of interacting electrons becomes exactly local in infinite dimensions; Georges and Kotliar mapped it onto a self-consistent quantum impurity problem, creating dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). For the first time, the Mott metal-insulator transition, the coexistence of quasiparticle and Hubbard bands, and the heavy-fermion state could be described non-perturbatively within one controlled framework. Combined with density-functional theory, DMFT became the standard predictive tool for correlated materials: transition-metal oxides, actinides such as plutonium, iron-based superconductors, and the magnetism and elasticity of iron at Earth-core conditions. Its spectra are quantitatively confirmed by photoemission and optical experiments worldwide. DMFT turned the physics of strong correlations from qualitative model studies into quantitative, first-principles materials theory, reshaping how we understand and design functional materials.
